title: How Long After Breast Augmentation Can I Drive? 1–2 Weeks
meta_description: Sources range from within 1 week to at least 2 weeks. Never on opioids or surgery day. Is day 3 too soon? What each source says, and the checks to make.
excerpt: Sources range from within 1 week to at least 2 weeks after breast augmentation, and you should never drive on opioid pain medicine or on surgery day. Here is what each source says, what to do about day 3, and the checks to make before your first drive.
quick_answer:
How long after breast augmentation can I drive?

Sources range from within 1 week to at least 2 weeks. University of Utah Health says most people are ready within one week, an article on the ASPS website says many women can after about a week, and MedlinePlus, which also covers lifts and reductions, says at least 2 weeks. Never on surgery day or on opioid pain medicine.

images.text_in_image:
When Can I Drive After Breast Augmentation?
Surgery day: No. Someone else drives you home.
Day 3: No source we read supports it. Only if your surgeon agrees.
Within 1 week: Most people are ready, University of Utah Health says.
About 1 week (7–10 days): Many women can drive, an article on the ASPS website says.
At least 2 weeks: What MedlinePlus says, on a page that also covers lifts and reductions.
Never on opioid pain medicine. Your surgeon decides.
Sources: University of Utah Health; article on the ASPS website; MedlinePlus; UW Medicine.
